career_stage.summary: Exercise neuroscience researcher with a PhD in Exercise Physiology, Marie Sklodowska-Curie postdoctoral fellowship experience, independent project leadership, human intervention research, stress biology, cognition and brain-health research exposure.

adjacent_domains: epigenetics related to stress and exercise
gut microbiota in lifestyle and health research

methods.evidence: Designed and conducted exercise and physical activity intervention studies across multiple populations, including randomized intervention work.

methods.name: randomized controlled trials
methods.evidence: Current and prior research includes randomized intervention design, implementation and outcome assessment.

methods.name: exercise and fitness assessment
methods.evidence: Background in exercise physiology, physical fitness assessment and training interventions.

methods.name: psychological and cognitive assessment
methods.evidence: Research includes well-being, stress, cognition and psychological outcomes in human studies.

methods.name: cortisol and HPA-axis related measurement
methods.evidence: Research experience includes cortisol and stress-biology outcomes and glucocorticoid-related work.

methods.evidence: Research collaborations and projects include MRI and brain-health outcomes; experience should not be interpreted as advanced independent fMRI preprocessing expertise.

methods.name: statistical analysis

research_experience: PhD research on exercise, hippocampal plasticity, glucocorticoid regulation and later brain health using animal models.
Postdoctoral and collaborative human research on exercise, physical activity, cognition, stress, brain health and lifestyle factors.
Marie Sklodowska-Curie postdoctoral fellowship leading the YoungFitT project at the University of Barcelona.
Independent and collaborative intervention research across young adults, older adults, children and other populations.
Research involving psychological stress, cortisol, cognition, MRI outcomes, epigenetic exposure, microbiota sampling and mixed-methods components.
Experience with scientific writing, protocol development, grant writing, project coordination, mentoring, dissemination and international collaboration.
transferable_strengths: Can transfer exercise-intervention expertise into adjacent health, behavioral, brain, stress and rehabilitation research when responsibilities are substantively aligned.
Can transfer stress-biology and psychophysiology experience into broader human stress, resilience, mental-health or behavioral medicine projects.
Can transfer intervention-design and trial-management experience into lifestyle, prevention and health-promotion research.
Can contribute to interdisciplinary teams where exercise or physical activity is one component rather than the job title itself.
Strong grant, project-management, supervision and international collaboration experience can support research-intensive roles beyond narrow laboratory labels.
hard_constraints: Do not treat roles requiring a medical degree, nursing degree or mandatory professional healthcare registration as eligible unless the vacancy explicitly allows an alternative qualification that this profile satisfies.
Do not treat advanced specialist methods explicitly required as mandatory if the profile only has exposure or DO_NOT_CLAIM status for that method.
Do not infer legal work authorization, citizenship, professional licensure or language proficiency that is not explicitly represented in the evidence available to the evaluator.
soft_preferences: Prefer research-intensive roles with substantive overlap in exercise, physical activity, brain health, stress, cognition, psychophysiology, human intervention research or closely adjacent health domains.
Interdisciplinary roles should remain in consideration when the actual responsibilities fit transferable expertise even if the title or department name does not exactly match the core domains.
Postdoctoral, research fellow, early faculty and research scientist roles are generally stronger targets than roles dominated by administration or unrelated teaching.
do_not_infer: advanced independent fMRI preprocessing or specialist neuroimaging analysis
advanced machine learning or AI research expertise
citizenship or unrestricted work authorization in any country

evaluation_guidance.recall_priority: Recall is more important than precision. When a role is plausibly relevant but evidence is incomplete or interdisciplinary, prefer REVIEW over an unjustified SKIP.
evaluation_guidance.transferable_fit: Evaluate whether responsibilities and essential criteria can realistically be satisfied through transferable research, intervention, stress-biology, exercise-science or quantitative experience. Do not require exact keyword overlap.
evaluation_guidance.title_handling: Job title alone is not decisive. Infer the actual scientific role from the full vacancy text, responsibilities and criteria before judging fit.
evaluation_guidance.eligibility_handling: Distinguish mandatory requirements from preferred ones. A preferred criterion should not become a hard blocker. If a mandatory criterion is ambiguous, represent uncertainty rather than inventing eligibility.
